results.translation: If one offers Me with love and devotion a leaf, a flower, a fruit or water, I will accept it.

results.title: Bhagavad-gītā As It Is 8.5
results.translation: And whoever, at the end of his life, quits his body remembering Me alone at once attains My nature. Of this there is no doubt.
results.purportStart: In this verse the importance of Kṛṣṇa consciousness is stressed. Anyone who quits his body in Kṛṣṇa consciousness is at once transferred to the transcendental nature of the Supreme Lord. The Supreme Lord is the purest of the pure. results.title: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam 3.15.19
results.translation: Although flowering plants like the mandāra, kunda, kurabaka, utpala, campaka, arṇa, punnāga, nāgakeśara, bakula, lily and pārijāta are full of transcendental fragrance, they are still conscious of the austerities performed by tulasī, for tulasī is given special preference by the Lord, who garlands Himself with tulasī leaves.
results.purportStart: The importance of tulasī leaves is very clearly mentioned here. Tulasī plants and their leaves are very important in devotional service. results.title: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam 2.3.23
results.translation: The person who has not at any time received the dust of the feet of the Lord’s pure devotee upon his head is certainly a dead body. And the person who has never experienced the aroma of the tulasī leaves from the lotus feet of the Lord is also a dead body, although breathing.
results.purportStart: According to Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī Ṭhākura, the breathing dead body is a ghost. When a man dies, he is called dead, but when he again appears in a subtle form not visible to our present vision and yet acts, such a dead body is called a ghost. results.title: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam 3.16.26
results.translation: The Lord replied: O brāhmaṇas, know that the punishment you inflicted on them was originally ordained by Me, and therefore they will fall to a birth in a demoniac family. But they will be firmly united with Me in thought through mental concentration intensified by anger, and they will return to My presence shortly.
results.purportStart: The Lord stated that the punishment inflicted by the sages upon the doorkeepers Jaya and Vijaya was conceived by the Lord Himself. Without the Lord’s sanction, nothing can happen. It is to be understood that there was a plan in the cursing of the Lord’s devotees in Vaikuṇṭha, and His plan is explained by many stalwart authorities. The Lord sometimes desires to fight. results.translation: The Lord then said to His attendants, Jaya and Vijaya: Depart this place, but fear not. All glories unto you. Though I am capable of nullifying the brāhmaṇas’ curse, I would not do so. On the contrary, it has My approval.
results.purportStart: As explained in connection with text 26, all the incidents that took place had the approval of the Lord. results.title: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam 3.16.31
results.translation: The Lord assured the two Vaikuṇṭha inhabitants, Jaya and Vijaya: By practicing the mystic yoga system in anger, you will be cleansed of the sin of disobeying the brāhmaṇas and within a very short time return to Me.
results.purportStart: The Supreme Personality of Godhead advised the two doorkeepers, Jaya and Vijaya, that by dint of bhakti-yoga in anger they would be delivered from the curses of the brāhmaṇas. Śrīla Madhva Muni remarks in this connection that by practicing bhakti-yoga one can become free from all sinful reactions. results.title: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam 5.5.26
results.translation: My dear sons, you should not envy any living entity — be he moving or nonmoving. Knowing that I am situated in them, you should offer respect to all of them at every moment. In this way, you offer respect to Me.
results.purportStart: In this verse the word vivikta-dṛgbhiḥ, meaning without envy, is used. All living entities are the abode of the Supreme Personality of Godhead in His Paramātmā feature. As confirmed in Brahma-saṁhitā: aṇḍāntara-sthaṁ paramāṇu-cayāntara-stham. The Lord is situated in this universe as Garbhodakaśāyī Viṣṇu and Kṣīrodakaśāyī Viṣṇu. He is also situated within every atom. results.title: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam 3.31.42
results.translation: A woman, therefore, should consider her husband, her house and her children to be the arrangement of the external energy of the Lord for her death, just as the sweet singing of the hunter is death for the deer.
results.purportStart: In these instructions of Lord Kapiladeva it is explained that not only is woman the gateway to hell for man, but man is also the gateway to hell for woman. It is a question of attachment. A man becomes attached to a woman because of her service, her beauty and many other assets, and similarly a woman becomes attached to a man for his giving her a nice place to live, ornaments, dress and children.

results.title: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam 10.34.25
results.translation: While Lord Kṛṣṇa and Lord Balarāma thus played according to Their own sweet will and sang to the point of apparent intoxication, a servant of Kuvera named Śaṅkhacūḍa came upon the scene.

results.title: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam 10.34.26
results.translation: O King, even as the two Lords looked on, Śaṅkhacūḍa brazenly began driving the women off toward the north. The women, who had accepted Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma as their Lords, began to cry out to Them.
results.purportStart: According to Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī, the demon Śaṅkhacūḍa shook a large stick at the beautiful young girls, thus frightening them and driving them toward the north. He did not actually touch them, as is corroborated by the following verse. results.title: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam 10.34.30
results.translation: Lord Govinda chased the demon wherever he ran, eager to take his crest jewel. Meanwhile Lord Balarāma stayed with the women to protect them.
results.purportStart: Śrīla Viśvanātha Cakravartī explains that the women were fatigued from being driven away, and thus Lord Balarāma protected them and consoled them as they rested. Meanwhile Lord Kṛṣṇa went after the demon. results.title: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam 10.34.31
results.translation: The mighty Lord overtook Śaṅkhacūḍa from a great distance as if from nearby, my dear King, and then with His fist the Lord removed the wicked demon’s head, together with his crest jewel.

results.title: Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam 9.19.14
results.translation: As supplying butter to a fire does not diminish the fire but instead increases it more and more, the endeavor to stop lusty desires by continual enjoyment can never be successful. [In fact, one must voluntarily cease from material desires.]
results.purportStart: One may have enough money and enough resources to satisfy the senses but still not be satisfied, for the endeavor to stop lusty desires by enjoying can never be successful. The example given here is very appropriate. One cannot stop a blazing fire by trying to extinguish it with butter. results.title: Bhagavad-gītā As It Is 3.39
results.translation: Thus the wise living entity’s pure consciousness becomes covered by his eternal enemy in the form of lust, which is never satisfied and which burns like fire.
results.purportStart: It is said in the Manu-smṛti that lust cannot be satisfied by any amount of sense enjoyment, just as fire is never extinguished by a constant supply of fuel. In the material world, the center of all activities is sex, and thus this material world is called maithunya-āgāra, or the shackles of sex life. 130: Once upon a time, I fainted through excess of enjoyments afforded to me by the society of Govinda in the sphere of the Rasa. Suddenly Radha turned up and saw me in that condition. Blinded with fury, she rebuked Krisna and cursed me saying, 'Vile one, avaunt; and take your birth as a human being'
In the Goloka, he was impatient with lust at your sight. But for fear of Rādhikā, he could not make you any advances there.
132: A good man, if he sees a virtuous woman alone, does not talk to her. Go away wherever you please. The Śrutis hold that only a vile man desires a woman. For she is sweet at first, but afterwards proves fatal to him. The mouth of a woman rains honey, but her heart is like a jar full of poison.
Naturally, she is lustful, harbours lust and enchants the mind.
133: She is an obstacle to the path of devotion, a hindrance to emancipation, an impediment to Hari's faith
Apparently, she wields beauty; but inwardly she is like a cup of ordure, urine, foul fume and polluted blood.

O goddess, your words are not wholly untrue. A part of your statement is true and a part, not true. God has divided the fair sex into two classes, viz., those who are chaste and those who may be easily seduced. The chaste woman is praise-worthy; the unchaste one should be condemned.
A virtuous man does not court the wife of another in public or in private; but I have come to you by Brahma's command to marry you according to the Gandharva rites.
A man subdued by a woman is unholy and contemptible.
134: a man subdued by his wife remains always impure
I tested your knowledge simply. A virtuous woman should wed a man after having tested him.
The demon Śankha-chuda began to enjoy the society of his love.
135: Both of them remained unsated. Their desire increased like fire fed with ghee.
136: He is devoted to me and was a valiant cowherd in his previous birth.
In the Goloka, he was one of my best attendants named Sudāma. He has become a demon by Radha's curse.
146: Hari, through the powers of his illusion, took the form of Śankha-chuda, approached Tulsi and violated her chastity.
The demon wisely laid aside his bow, adopted a posture of meditation and remembered Hari.
147: Hari, in order to accomplish the design of the gods, took the form of Śankha-chuda and cohabited with Tulsi.
O Lord of dissemblers, who are you? You have violated my chastity. I must, therefore, curse you, whoever you are.

Lord, you are unkind to me and possess a heart of stone. You have fraudulently violated me and killed my husband. As you are hard-hearted like a stone, you will be worshipped in the world in the form of a stone. Those who call you merciful are deluded.
I should now give you the fruits of your own austerities.
You should now quit your body, take a celestial form and revel with me like Ramā.
148: Hari will not be so much pleased with the gift of a thousand jars full of honey as with the offer of a Tulsi leaf.
I, too, by your curse, will turn into a stone on the coast of the Gandaki.
